title: Inserting a short chord at any two positions gives Knuth equivalent matchings
author: Avichai Marmor
work: Schur-positivity of short chords in matchings
difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 1157-1160: for a matching m and any two insertion positions i and j, the matchings obtained by inserting a short chord at i and at j are Knuth equivalent. The proof (source lines 1161-1165) is an induction on the distance between the two positions, and its only non-formal step is the claim that inserting at i+1 is Knuth equivalent to inserting at i; that claim has to be read off the explicit vertex-shifting formula of the insertion definition rather than from the statement, and it is what makes the induction run. The statement records neither the induction parameter nor the appeal to the shifting formula.
